details: False for finite classes under the message-free definition. On #classes/balanced_six_split, proper equivalence-query complexity is 3 but no proper unlabeled compression scheme exists, even without stability. Thus psUSC is $+\infty$, and no finite-valued function of $Q_{\mathrm{peq}}$ universally bounds psUSC. The exact inequality also fails when psUSC is finite: #classes/k4_incidence_with_empty has $Q_{\mathrm{peq}}=2$ and $\mathrm{pUSC}=\mathrm{psUSC}=3$. This additional finite witness does not refute an affine or unspecified functional bound restricted to finite psUSC.
proof_source: Survey Corollary cor:balanced-six-split-nonexistence gives universal nonexistence-based refutation. Corollary cor:finite-proper-query-counterexample gives the separate finite-valued 3-versus-2 refutation, with the full benchmark proof owned by the database.
witness_verification: Values 1183 and 1185 give $Q_{\mathrm{peq}}=3$ and $\mathrm{psUSC}=+\infty$. Nonexistence on this fixed finite class refutes every finite upper bound, in particular every proposed affine bound. This is stronger than a growing finite ratio and is not an asymptotic-family claim.
name: Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity / Proper Stable Sample Compression
